evidence.exact_quote: Runtime alert lifecycle defines `/auto-resolution`: an alert may auto-resolve on healthy refresh, downgrade to historical `/seen` after acknowledgment, and clear badges consistently across mirrored surfaces. Persistent non-blocking issues support `per-alert` `acknowledge`, `snooze`, and `/snooze/mute`; `mute by root_cause_key` is allowed only where safe. A mute or snooze must not suppress blocking confirmations or `security-sensitive` failures, and muted issues remain visible in owning surfaces while stopping repeated interruptions.

items.impact: Provides a shared, auditable lifecycle and prevents muting from hiding blocking or security-sensitive failures.
items.statement: Alert auto-resolution, acknowledgment, snooze, mute, mirrored badge clearing, and non-suppressible blocking/security behavior are explicitly contracted.
items.title: Shared alert lifecycle is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - queued messages are FIFO with max 2 entries, transient, and not restart-persisted
- queue item states are `pending | in_progress | completed | blocked | skipped`; `superseded` is plan-level only and not a queue item state

items.impact: Bounds queue growth and prevents the UI from falsely restoring transient submissions after restart.
items.statement: The chat queue has a closed state set, FIFO order, a two-entry limit, and an explicit non-persistence boundary.
items.title: Composer queue semantics are bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - merge strategy for project state when multiple durable sources contribute

items.impact: Implementations can choose incompatible precedence, conflict, retry, and rollback rules, producing nondeterministic project projections under concurrent durable updates.
items.statement: Project-state merging is named but no merge operator, source precedence, version check, conflict representation, atomicity boundary, or recovery oracle is defined.
items.title: Project-state merge strategy is not executable

evidence.exact_quote: Per-target control state is closed to:
- `projection_failed` means PM could not generate or write the target projection and must expose repair/retry actions without pretending the target is current.

items.impact: Prevents provider-native projections from appearing synchronized when PM has lost control or a write failed.
items.statement: Agent-Config closes each projection target to controlled, manual_override, or projection_failed and requires truthful failure UI.
items.title: Instruction projection authority is visible

evidence.exact_quote: - polling is acceptable for external systems that do not provide push updates, such as GitHub Actions status checks; those intervals are freshness aids only and must not become the correctness model for the rest of the shell

items.impact: External status can remain indefinitely stale or poll too aggressively because no interval bounds, backoff, jitter, stale deadline, or offline transition is testable.
items.statement: The external polling exception lacks an operational freshness and network-loss contract.
items.title: External polling has no bounded freshness policy

evidence.exact_quote: Slint's screen reader support is limited. Mitigations:
- Set `accessible-role` and `accessible-label` properties on all interactive components where available in current stable Slint

items.impact: Builders cannot determine which controls may ship without semantics or how unsupported screen-reader behavior is disclosed and tested per platform.
items.statement: Screen-reader mitigation is conditional on framework availability but has no minimum supported-role matrix, platform test harness, pass threshold, or release-blocking rule.
items.title: Screen-reader support lacks a release oracle

evidence.exact_quote: - `editor_unsaved_buffer.v1:*` stores local unsaved buffer state only and MUST NOT imply that a remote write succeeded.

items.impact: Separates recoverable local editing state from remote durability and avoids misleading save-success claims.
items.statement: The unsaved-buffer persistence record is explicitly non-authoritative for remote write success.
items.title: Unsaved-buffer authority boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Hidden views have zero runtime cost. Widget trees are destroyed when the condition becomes false and recreated when true.

items.impact: Unsaved transient values, focus, selection, in-flight feedback, or accessibility announcements can disappear during navigation unless every retained field is externally modeled.
items.statement: Conditional view destruction is mandated without an inventory of state that must be hoisted before teardown or an oracle proving recreation is lossless.
items.title: Lazy view teardown has an undefined state boundary

evidence.exact_quote: - terminal sessions restore only as verified-live or historical records; Puppet Master MUST NOT fake live PTY continuity after restart
- canonical recovery outcomes are `restored_live`, `restored_exited`, `restored_disconnected`, and `restored_without_history`

items.impact: Users can distinguish restored structure and history from proof of a live terminal session.
items.statement: Terminal crash recovery has a closed outcome vocabulary and forbids invented PTY continuity.
items.title: Terminal recovery is truth-preserving

evidence.exact_quote: Clipboard migration gate status is **PASS** only when all required criteria below are true.
- [ ] No custom text-widget clipboard handler remains in the migration target.

items.impact: Creates a falsifiable all-required migration gate spanning native editable and read-only clipboard behavior.
items.statement: Clipboard migration has an explicit conjunctive pass gate and forbids legacy custom text clipboard handlers.
items.title: Clipboard migration gate is testable

evidence.exact_quote: - Drag-to-swap is upgraded to **drag-to-reorder** within the grid. Widgets can also be **resized** by dragging their edges (grid-snapping, per Plans/Widget_System.md section 3).

| **Dashboard card drag-and-drop** | Medium | Drag-reorder logic for dashboard cards is custom and complex. Mitigation: Use a simple ordered-list model with drag-handle + click-to-swap as MVP; full drag-and-drop is enhancement. Test with varying card counts (2-12). |

items.impact: A builder can ship click-to-swap without resize or can treat drag-to-reorder and resize as required, so MVP completion is not uniquely decidable.
items.statement: The risk mitigation defers full dashboard drag-and-drop while Appendix C normatively upgrades MVP to drag-to-reorder and edge resizing.
items.title: Dashboard interaction scope contradicts itself

evidence.exact_quote: Widget_System consumes this named catalog directly; it does not invent new widget IDs or synthesize missing entries.

- **Plans/Widget_System.md section 2** = **composed page widgets**: OrchestratorStatus, BudgetDonuts, NodeTree, LedgerTable, and other content panels built FROM atomic components. These are the widgets users can add/remove/move/resize on the Dashboard, Usage page, and Orchestrator `Progress` only.

items.impact: Dashboard consumers cannot determine whether non-named composed widgets are selectable, undermining stable IDs, migration, and add-widget validation.
items.statement: Appendix C restricts Dashboard selection to owner-promoted named entries but later describes the broader composed catalog as addable on Dashboard.
items.title: Dashboard widget catalog authority is ambiguous

evidence.exact_quote: 3. **No React/Tauri/DOM-rendered product UI or HTML/CSS/JS product shell** -- native desktop is Rust + Slint `.slint` markup; Slint/WASM web may use only minimal HTML/canvas bootstrap and generated/minimal JavaScript glue needed to load the WASM canvas client

items.impact: Prevents implementation-reference web patterns from becoming an alternate product-shell authority while retaining a bounded WASM bootstrap path.
items.statement: The native product-shell technology boundary and the narrow Slint/WASM exception are locked.
items.title: Native UI stack boundary is closed

evidence.exact_quote: - Every disclosure must include: control name, requested value, effective value (if any), and human-readable reason.
- When a limitation is only discovered at runtime, surface the disclosure inline on the active surface **and** persist the same information in run detail/history so it is auditable later.

items.impact: Prevents provider limitations from being silently represented as honored Persona behavior and preserves later auditability.
items.statement: Persona control disclosures carry requested/effective values and reason, and runtime-discovered limitations propagate into history.
items.title: Persona provider-gap disclosure is durable

evidence.exact_quote: These editors should also allow platform/model selection per mapping and show compatibility warnings.

items.impact: Different surfaces can omit platform/model mapping or resolve overlapping defaults differently, making effective runtime identity unpredictable.
items.statement: Persona mapping editors use non-normative 'should' language and do not define precedence when stage, pass, node, package, lane, seam, and user overrides overlap.
items.title: Persona mapping precedence is unresolved

evidence.exact_quote: - Browser and agent-debugging UX follows the Section15 built-in browser contract rather than `web_search`, `web_fetch`, Site Reader, or raw CDP. The GUI presents the PM-managed CEF runtime, DevTools, visible `automation_session` / `auth_session` surfaces, `/video` evidence, `browser_selection_context`, and `browser_element_context`; capture chips must not auto-send, advanced storage or `/cookie` changes require explicit confirmation, and takeover controls expose pause, `/continue/stop`, and resume as named actions.

items.impact: Makes browser evidence sharing and powerful storage/takeover operations visible and confirmation-gated.
items.statement: The browser GUI separates managed sessions from web tools and requires explicit send, confirmation, and named takeover controls.
items.title: Browser control is least-privilege and visible

evidence.exact_quote: - setup, Doctor, update, and installer surfaces must disclose a selected CEF path's roughly ~1 GB app-size impact and provide remediation when runtime install/update verification fails
- when the bundled browser runtime is damaged or unavailable, the UI must surface `runtime_unavailable` with remediation and keep source/native surfaces usable

items.impact: Install/update failure behavior can diverge on disk-space exhaustion, interrupted updates, corrupt runtimes, rollback, concurrent sessions, and offline repair.
items.statement: The bundled browser runtime requires disclosure and remediation but does not specify storage thresholds, atomic update/rollback, version retention, retry ceilings, or a verification oracle.
items.title: CEF runtime lifecycle is not operationally closed

evidence.exact_quote: - deterministic annotation re-anchoring after edits
- no silent annotation loss

items.impact: Overlapping edits, duplicated text, deleted anchors, concurrent revisions, or source-map changes can produce divergent attachment or silent misattachment despite the stated goal.
items.statement: Deterministic re-anchoring and no-loss behavior are required without an anchor identity algorithm, ambiguity state, conflict UI, or pass/fail corpus.
items.title: Annotation re-anchoring is asserted, not specified

evidence.exact_quote: When Assistant Chat or Deep Plan recommends the Planning Wizard, show a visible recommendation card rather than silently switching surfaces.
- Do not silently redirect the user from chat into the wizard.

items.impact: Preserves user authority over a major workflow transition and makes context transfer explicit.
items.statement: Assistant-to-Wizard handoff is recommendation-and-consent based, never a silent redirect.
items.title: Wizard handoff requires visible consent

evidence.exact_quote: - canonical labels: `Light`, `Balanced`, `Comprehensive`
- tooltip/help copy must explain that Deep Plan is more intensive than Plan at the same PT

items.impact: Localized builds may translate stored identity, fail to translate help, overflow compact controls, or lose canonical-value round trips.
items.statement: Planning UX fixes English labels and required copy but does not separate stable enum values from localized display strings or define fallback and layout-expansion behavior.
items.title: Planning controls lack localization semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - blocked episodes remain distinct when more than one is active
The GUI does not synthesize alternate blocked schemas, alternate action arrays, or alternate retry classes for specific surfaces.

items.impact: Prevents surface-specific blocked-state drift and preserves control over simultaneous recovery episodes.
items.statement: Canonical blocked UI preserves multiple episode identities and forbids local schema, action-array, or retry-class forks.
items.title: Blocked-state taxonomy is shared and multi-episode

evidence.exact_quote: Until owner runtime contracts define dedicated all-blocked events, GUI surfaces MAY derive all-blocked banners from current projections but MUST NOT treat undeclared runtime events as canonical.

items.impact: Different consumers can disagree on whether a run is all-blocked, creating inconsistent banners and escalation without violating the text.
items.statement: Temporary all-blocked derivation is permitted but the projection set, snapshot consistency, elapsed-time boundary, and false-positive suppression rule are undefined.
items.title: All-blocked derivation is not deterministic

Reviewed persistence boundaries, Agent-Config authority, confirmation and approval patterns, event-driven refresh, anti-flicker, responsive behavior, and accessibility limitations and oracles.
Reviewed Slint/Rust organization, view lifecycle, list virtualization, persistence keys, startup and crash restore, migration mappings, and the clipboard migration gate.
Reviewed risk mitigations, promoted MVP scope, cross-reference and locked-decision authority, Dashboard widget catalog and migration, Persona compatibility, runtime disclosure, and mapping editors.

Reviewed browser/session security and hosting, rendering surfaces, performance/accessibility, Assistant planning and Wizard handoff, annotation revision, compatibility lineage, and canonical blocked/recovery behavior.
